body:
Sketch, not a plan: a fourth list kind where a household shares out chores and sees who is pulling their weight. Deliberately blocked — the shape below needs a proper design discussion first, especially the social half.

## Why it fits here

It is the ledger with points instead of money. An entry is a COMPLETED chore, the way a ledger entry is a movement of money: `done_by` plays the part of `paid_by`, the shares play the part of `paid_for`, and the balance — what you have earned minus your share of the household's work — is the same arithmetic, summing to zero over the list. The Balances screen, the shared case table and the settle-up algorithm all carry over; "settle up" becomes "the chores you should take next". Confirmation has a precedent too: close_votes is already "this is not final until the right people agree".

## Shape

* Kind `chores`. Items are completions, not chore definitions; the chore CATALOGUE is the registry, which already remembers a name (plus, here, its default points) per list.
* One new item field, mirroring `expense`:
  `"chore": {"done_by": "<account>", "shares": {"<account>": 3, ...}, "points": 3, "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "confirmed_by": ["<account>"]}`
  Points are integers, so none of the cent arithmetic applies.
* Balance = earned - share, derived and never stored, exactly as the ledger's is.

## Rules

* A completion counts once it is confirmed. **The doer may confirm their own**, which is what keeps the whole thing out of deadlock — the alternative (somebody else must confirm) means an unconfirmed pile and a person who feels cheated. A second member's confirmation is then a stronger signal, not a requirement; whether the UI distinguishes "self-confirmed" from "confirmed by someone else" is an open question.
* Optionally auto-confirm after n days, as a list setting.
* Points and `done_by` freeze once confirmed — the existing freeze rule with confirmation as the trigger instead of a close vote.
* Changing a chore's default points never rewrites past entries, like a ledger's fixed currency.

## Screens

Entries (what was done, by whom, confirmed or pending) and Balances (your points against your share). A per-list switch turns scoring off and leaves just the log, for households that want the rota without the score.

## The part that needs discussion, not code

Scores between housemates are socially loaded: a leaderboard is an efficient way to make whoever is behind stop opening the app. The ledger's framing is the safer one — "you are 8 points below your share" rather than "Alice 47, Bob 12". Worth deciding before anything is built.

## Open questions

* Does the balance reset weekly or run forever?
* Are points per chore, or per member-hour?
* Does an unconfirmed completion show as pending-and-counted, or not count at all?
* Recurrence (chores that come back) and automatic assignment are separate features; v1 should be log, confirm, balance, and nothing else.
title: Chores with scores: a fourth list kind, the ledger with points instead of money
